gap: No result ChatGPT got states, for any wireless board in its answer other than the RK61 (ATK A87, Rosewill Neon S75, Redragon K530 Pro, Redragon K526 Pro, DAREU FLEX75), how many Bluetooth devices it pairs, whether its sockets take 3-pin or 5-pin switches, or which operating systems its wireless modes and software support; I could not open any maker page to fill those cells, so this is a gap in the rivals, not a sourced finding.
standout_why: I opened mkbguide.com and rottenwifi.com (both cited), plus mechvibes.com and official.deals/under-50. Between them they cover compatibility for the RK61 only: three Bluetooth devices and 3-pin/5-pin sockets (Mechvibes), and hot-swap only on the current tri-mode revision (MKB Guide). Rotten WiFi gives no OS support for its seven picks and calls K530 Pro hot-swap only 'reported'. Official.Deals has titles and prices only. None covers the ATK A87, Rosewill Neon S75, DAREU FLEX75, Redragon K526 Pro, Gamakay TK101 or Gamakay NS68. The score is 1, not 2, because every maker page I tried was blocked, so I have no maker-sourced cell to put against them.
decides: It does not decide the pick yet. None of the keyboards we already link is under $50; the only partner boards under the line are the Gamakay TK101 at $47.99 and the NS68 tri-mode at $39.99 (your table, read 2026-11-21), and neither has a record. A compatibility row for either needs Gamakay's own page or manual read first: Bluetooth device count, Win/Mac switch, socket pin count, and for the NS68 whether the sockets take only magnetic switches and what polling rate and rapid trigger it keeps on 2.4 GHz and Bluetooth. If those are read, the angle could separate the TK101 (the only board here with a number pad) from the ATK A87 and the RK61, whose compatibility the rivals already cover.
